first_impression.reaction: I googled this half expecting a Pinterest dump of macaron tags. The intro is calm and the line about 'practical checks that decide whether it holds up on the night' is what kept me. That's what I actually want: not twenty cute ideas, but which ones fall over when it's windy or Nan can't read the card. I skimmed the ideas, then properly read the practical and destination sections.

journey.quote: The ideas below are grouped by what the guest does at the display, and each one comes with the practical checks that decide whether it holds up on the night.
journey.reaction: Good. This tells me it isn't just a mood board. Earned the scroll.

journey.section: Finish the Table Plan Before You Choose a Display
journey.quote: Build it in Wonderland Studio, our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, so the list you send to the stationer or the screen is the same list your RSVPs produced.
journey.reaction: Fair point, and frankly anything that means we aren't reconciling three spreadsheets at 11pm is appealing. Four links in one paragraph is a bit much though; it starts to feel like a link farm.

journey.quote: Choose something that fits in a carry-on if guests are flying home.
journey.reaction: Half our guests are flying in. Small thing, but it's the kind of detail that tells me whoever wrote this has actually thought about a destination wedding.

journey.quote: Few things welcome a guest more warmly than a glass with their name on it.
journey.reaction: Slightly gushing, but the next bit about staff pouring in time and a non-alcoholic option rescues it.

journey.quote: Pair it with a plain alphabetical list to one side so nobody has to hunt across continents for their name.
journey.reaction: This is the one I'd send James. Personal, not resort-package, and it comes with the sensible caveat. Honest trade-off.
I didn't know what this heading meant until I read it, and then it was mostly the mirror idea again plus a photo spot. Felt like filler.

journey.section: A Screen or QR Lookup on Arrival
journey.quote: Never rely on a phone alone. Some guests will not have one to hand, some will have a flat battery, and signal at a remote venue can be patchy.
journey.reaction: Exactly my grandparents. I trust a page more when it tells me where the trendy option fails.

journey.quote: Queensland guidance for events is a sound reference here.
journey.reaction: Why Queensland? We're in Sydney and probably marrying in Europe. The advice underneath is sensible, but the opener makes it feel pasted in, and the paragraph reads like a government PDF. The last paragraph, the practical one, is the bit I actually needed.

journey.quote: In practice, that means an interactive display should never be the only way to find a seat. Keep a printed list at a seated reading height, and ask a host or a member of the bridal party to stand nearby for the first half hour.
journey.reaction: This is the useful line. It's what I'd forward to Mum.

journey.quote: give one person the master list on the day so every change goes through them.
journey.reaction: Right, but who is that person at a wedding overseas? If it's me or my sister, that's the opposite of what we want. The page doesn't say whether that's something the Advisor or anyone on the ground covers.

journey.section: Interactive Seating Charts at a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Setup windows, outdoor display rules and power access are details to confirm with the venue directly. Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these answers are settled before the design is.
journey.reaction: The checklist above is great, real insider stuff. But these two sentences pull against each other: first it sounds like I'm chasing the venue myself, then it says the Advisor confirms things in writing. Which is it? That's exactly the 'what does end-to-end actually mean' question.

journey.section: Plan It with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: our Wedded Concierge service pairs you with one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: One named person, start to finish, is the reassurance I'm looking for. Not a hard sell either, which I appreciate.

unanswered_questions: On the day itself, is anyone from Wedded Wonderland or the Advisor's team physically there, or is the 'one person with the master list' going to be a family member?
Does the Advisor brief the venue on the seating display (setup, pack-down, storage of pieces sent ahead), or do we liaise with the venue ourselves?
Are there any real weddings you've done where one of these displays was used, with the venue and date? I'd like to see one that actually happened.
Does Wonderland Studio cost anything, and does the Advisor see our table plan in it?

turn_offs_found.quote: Few things welcome a guest more warmly than a glass with their name on it.
turn_offs_found.why: Mildly sugary, magazine-filler phrasing. Not a deal-breaker, but it's the one line that sounds like copy rather than advice.

would_share_with: James (partner), for the map seating chart idea and the destination checklist
Mum, for the accessibility and printed-list advice, because she will worry about the grandparents

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start a conversation with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: Low-pressure and I like the single-point-of-contact line. But this is a seating chart post and we haven't picked a country yet; I'd want to read a couple more posts and see a real wedding before I talk to anyone. If the page had been clearer on who handles the venue liaison and the day itself, I'd be closer to yes.

top_3_changes: Resolve the who-does-what tension in the destination section. Old: "Setup windows, outdoor display rules and power access are details to confirm with the venue directly." New: "Setup windows, outdoor display rules and power access are details the venue has to confirm directly."

Drop the random-feeling state reference in the accessibility opener. Old: "Queensland guidance for events is a sound reference here." New: "Australian government guidance on accessible events is a useful reference here, wherever you marry." (Keeps the existing Queensland link and facts unchanged.)
Make the vague heading say what it is. Old: "### The Art of Technology" New: "### A Seating Chart That Doubles as a Photo Spot"

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), judging only what matters to this persona
No invented brand facts; gaps about on-the-day presence, venue liaison, real weddings and Wonderland Studio cost logged as unanswered questions
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings and add no new facts, fees, commissions, supplier sourcing or vetting claims, or measurements
HTML comments and image slot notes treated as invisible

open_questions.question: The draft never says who on the ground holds the master list or liaises with the venue on the day. The planner_couple persona's main fear is 'no one accountable on the day'. Should the editor clarify the Advisor's role here using existing approved brand wording only?

assumptions: Reader is Sophie, reading on her phone after a Google search, 14 months out with no destination chosen.

The 'Australian government guidance' wording in change 2 is an assumption that the editor is comfortable describing the Queensland Government guide that way; if not, keep a neutral phrase such as 'Government guidance on accessible events'.
